about.metaDescription: Polaris is a self-hosted control plane for files, tasks, deployments and game servers.
about.intro: A self-hosted control plane. One place to keep files, run tasks, deploy applications and manage game servers, on hardware its operator owns rather than on somebody else's service. This is one such deployment, run by the person or organization that installed it.
about.account: Everything past this page needs an account here, which its operator hands out. There is nothing to sign up for.

connecting.title: Connecting an account
connecting.body: People with an account here can connect outside accounts of their own, and each connection asks for the least it can. A connected Google account is read-only, and only so the calendar can be shown beside the tasks - Polaris cannot change or delete anything in it. Microsoft and Dropbox are limited to the folder Polaris creates for backups. Steam, Epic Games and Minecraft hand over an account id and a display name, so a game server can tell one player from another, and no credential at all. Discord hands over those, the address on the account, and the names of the servers it is in - nothing inside them, and never the ability to post as you.
connecting.owner: Connecting is always started by the account's owner, and unlinking it here destroys the credential and the access with it. The <link>privacy policy</link> sets out what is stored and for how long.

software.title: The software
software.body: Polaris is free software, published under the GNU AGPL-3.0 license. The people who write it operate no service and never see this deployment: it runs entirely on its operator's own machine.
